title: Reputation, Disclosure, and the Scope of Entry
abstract: arXiv:2510.21759v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: An entrant deciding how widely to launch takes into account both an incumbent's ability to respond and what its earlier conduct reveals about that ability. We develop a two-market Cournot model in which competitive responses use resources shared across markets. Entry into a second market weakens the response in the first and can make one-market entry unattractive. Greater disclosure of an earlier response encourages a less capable incumbent to imitate a more capable one. Conditional on observing a response, the later entrant therefore expands more often, although aggregate entry probabilities remain continuous. We then compare disclosure of conduct with a public audit of capability. translated_title: 声誉、信息披露与进入范围
translated_abstract: arXiv:2510.21759v4 公告类型：替换 摘要：一个决定进入市场范围的进入者会同时考虑在位者做出竞争反应的能力，以及该在位者此前行为所透露的关于其能力的信息。我们构建了一个双市场古诺模型，其中竞争性反应需要使用跨市场共享的资源。进入第二个市场会削弱在位者在第一个市场的反应能力，并可能使单一市场进入变得不具吸引力。对早期反应的更大程度披露会促使能力较低的在位者模仿能力较高的在位者。因此，在观察到反应的条件下，后来的进入者会更频繁地扩大进入范围，尽管总体进入概率保持连续。随后，我们将行为信息披露与对能力的公开审计进行比较。对于具有统一进入成本的一组开放参数，当发布成本较低时，完全的行为披露在该政策类别内能最大化总剩余；而在保持所有早期进入者和单一市场进入者不变的可分离反应成本下，不披露才是最优的。
tldr: 本文构建了一个竞争性反应消耗跨市场共享资源的双市场古诺模型，揭示行为信息披露会诱使低能力在位者模仿高能力者从而改变进入者的扩张行为，并证明行为披露与能力公开审计在不同成本结构下的福利效应存在差异。
en_tdlr: The paper develops a two-market Cournot model in which competitive responses draw on shared cross-market resources, showing that conduct disclosure induces less capable incumbents to mimic more capable ones and thereby alters entrants' expansion behavior, while comparing the welfare effects of conduct disclosure versus public capability audits under different cost structures.
